headline: Before the History Books
subtitle: Match the leader to the strange fact
clue: Lived in Harlem and wrote about Black racial oppression
fact: The New York Times' 1969 obituary says he 'is believed to have lived in Harlem for a while' (c. 1912–13; only a New York letter survives). In 1924 he wrote essays on lynching and 'the Black race'.

clue: Was an army cook's assistant, then his country's light heavyweight boxing champion
fact: Amin joined the King's African Rifles as an assistant cook in 1946 and was Uganda's light heavyweight boxing champion from 1951 to 1960.
original_clue: Was a cook's assistant, then a heavyweight boxing champion

clue: Published a children's poetry book a decade before the genocide he was convicted of
fact: Karadžić, a psychiatrist and poet, published the children's poems 'Ima čuda – nema čuda' (1984). The UN tribunal (ICTY) convicted him in 2016 of genocide at Srebrenica (1995); on appeal in 2019 his sentence became life.
original_clue: Wrote children's books before committing genocide

clue: Worked in French factories, including a Renault car plant, from age 16 to 21
fact: Deng reached France in Oct 1920 aged 16 and left for Moscow in Jan 1926 aged 21. He worked at the Schneider steelworks in Le Creusot, a Hutchinson rubber plant and as a fitter at Renault in Billancourt.
original_clue: Worked at a car-making factory in France from when he was 16 to 21

clue: Slept in a Star Trek-themed bedroom in Iowa when he was there learning about agriculture
fact: In 1985 Xi led a five-man agricultural delegation from Hebei to Iowa and stayed with a family in Muscatine, in their son's Star Trek-themed room.

clue: Took dance and violin lessons in London to try to fit in with the cool kids
fact: As a law student in London (1888–91) Gandhi bought a top hat and a Bond Street suit and took dancing, violin and elocution lessons to become an 'English gentleman', then quit after about three months.
source_name: Gandhi, The Story of My Experiments with Truth

clue: Avoided meat and alcohol, partly hoping to ease his chronic gas
fact: Hitler had lifelong cramps and flatulence and went meat-free in the late 1930s; his motives are debated, he did eat meat and drink beer or wine at times, and his doctors noted the diet made the gas worse.
original_clue: Never drank or ate meat, but mostly because it gave him bad farts

headline: Of Age
subtitle: Age of consent (with an adult who isn't a teacher or guardian)
clue: 14, or 16 if the adult is a teacher or guardian
fact: Italy's Penal Code (art. 609-quater) sets 14, rising to 16 when the older partner is a parent, guardian, teacher or anyone else the minor is entrusted to.
source_name: Wikipedia: Age of consent by country (Italian Penal Code art. 609-quater)

clue: 16, 17 or 18, depending on the state
fact: There is no single national age: each state sets its own, 16 in many states and 17 or 18 in others (US Department of Health and Human Services guide to state laws).
source_name: US HHS (ASPE): Statutory Rape, A Guide to State Laws

clue: 16 nationally since 2023, though local youth ordinances are often seen as making it 18
fact: In 2023 Japan raised its national age of consent from 13, unchanged since 1907, to 16. Regional ordinances banning 'lewd' acts with minors under 18 are often seen as raising it to 18 in practice.
Slovenia's Criminal Code sets the age of consent at 15, the same for everyone.
source_name: Wikipedia: Age of consent by country

fact: Ireland's Criminal Law (Sexual Offences) Act 2006 sets the age of consent at 17, one of the highest in Europe.
source_name: Irish Statute Book: Criminal Law (Sexual Offences) Act 2006

clue: 21, unless the couple are married
fact: Bahrain's Penal Code (art. 345) punishes consensual sex with a female under 21; within marriage the age is 16.
source_name: Penal Code of Bahrain (1976, as amended), via UNODC

clue: 14, but 21 for same-sex relations
fact: Madagascar's Penal Code (art. 331) sets 14, but makes an 'indecent or unnatural act' with a same-sex partner under 21 a crime.
source_name: Wikipedia: Age of consent by country (Madagascar Penal Code of 1972, art. 331)

headline: Hard Line
subtitle: Penalties in law for raping a child
clue: At least 5 years (up to 20) for a child under 16
fact: Penal Code art. 177 (revised 2023): non-consensual intercourse, which includes any intercourse with a child under 16 (13-15 if the adult is 5+ years older), carries a fixed term of at least 5 years; art. 12 caps fixed terms at 20.
source_name: e-Gov: Penal Code (Act No. 45 of 1907), art. 177
note: These are the penalties written in each country's law for the main child-rape offence, not the sentences courts actually hand down; age bands, aggravating factors and sentencing practice differ a lot.

clue: At least 20 years for a child under 16, and death is possible in aggravated cases
fact: POCSO Act as amended in 2019: penetrative sexual assault on a child under 16 is at least 20 years up to life (s.4(2)); aggravated cases, e.g. a child under 12, are at least 20 years, life for the rest of natural life, or death (s.6).

clue: Death or life in prison, and nothing lighter, for raping a minor
fact: Penal Code s.376(3) (added 2016): rape of a minor is punished with death or imprisonment for life, plus a fine. A 2021 bill's chemical-castration clause was dropped before it passed.

clue: Up to 16 years for a child under 14, and at least a quarter of that unless the judge records special reasons
fact: Penal Law 5737-1977 s.345: sex with a child under 14 is rape even with 'consent' (16 years; 20 if aggravated, e.g. force on a child under 16). s.355 sets a minimum of one quarter of the maximum unless the court records special reasons. Death is not available.

clue: Up to 15 years, or just a fine, for a child under 12; no minimum
fact: Criminal Code art. 250 (Sexual Offences Act, in force 1 July 2024): penetration of a child under 12 carries up to 15 years or a fifth-category fine, with no statutory minimum; ages 12-15 are up to 12 years (art. 248).

clue: 1 to 5 years for sex with a child under 12 when no force is used
fact: Criminal Code art. 187 (revised 1 July 2024): a sexual act with a child under 12 is 1 to 5 years; under 16, up to 5 years or a monetary penalty. If force or coercion is used, rape (art. 190) is 1 to 10 years.
